snippet.description:
UPSC Preparation in College or After Graduation? The Real Problem Is How You Prepare.

Earlier, a common path to UPSC preparation was to finish college and then move to Delhi for a dedicated foundation course. With the rise of online UPSC coaching, YouTube, learning platforms and digital resources, many students now begin their UPSC preparation while still in college.

But does starting early automatically mean better preparation?

In this short from the LevelUp IAS GS Foundation Course for UPSC CSE 2028, the discussion looks at the real challenge: not whether you start UPSC preparation in college or after graduation, but whether you can consistently follow the complete preparation process.

For UPSC beginners, starting early can help build conceptual clarity and give more time for GS preparation, Prelims, Mains, Current Affairs, Answer Writing, CSAT, tests, revision and mentorship. The LevelUp IAS GS Foundation 2028 is designed as an integrated program for college students, working professionals and first-time UPSC aspirants, with Prelims and Mains preparation connected from the beginning.

The key is not simply “start early.” It is to start systematically and stay consistent.
